metadata.title: Quantification of CAR T cell performance against acute leukemia using Bayesian inference - code
metadata.description:
# Quantification of CAR T cell performance against acute leukemia using Bayesian inference
 
Download `CAR T cell performance.zip` and `data.zip`; and unzip them. Place the `data` folder inside the `CAR T cell performance` folder. Ensure `CAR T cell performance` contains `Qured.jl` and `DiffEqBayes.jl` folders.

**This project requires Qured.jl and forked DiffEqBayes.jl julia packages. If they were not supplied with this repo, contact Saumil Shah. email: shah[at]evolbio.mpg.de**

This project aims to find the most appropriate functional form for CAR T cell expansion and quantify the performance of different CAR T cell constructs. Please refer to the corresponding manuscript for more details.

## Installation
This project uses Julia v1.9. We recommend `juliaup` to install Julia. Please follow the installation instructions at [`juliaup` repo](https://github.com/JuliaLang/juliaup).
Install Julia v1.9 using `juliaup`:
```sh
juliaup add 1.9
juliaup default 1.9
julia --version
```

### Julia
Run this in the root repo directory to set up the Julia environment and get dependencies.
```sh
julia
]
activate .
instantiate
precompile
```

Make sure that the julia environment was instantiated without any errors. Please also ensure that the `Qured` and `DiffEqBayes` packages appear as follows. This is important because of these local dev packages.
```sh
[ebbdde9d] DiffEqBayes v3.6.2 `DiffEqBayes.jl`
[f728bd8c] Qured v0.1.4 `Qured.jl`
```

## Where to start
The `example.jl` takes an integer command-line argument between 1-5 for one of the 5 CAR T cell constructs. You can call it in the following manner for CD123w inference:
```sh
julia -t auto example.jl 4
```
It will then output a `.jld2` binary file that contains a `2x2x8x4` julia `NamedArray`. The dimensions correspond to 2 effectors, 2 targets, 8 candidate models, and 4 initial conditions or ratios. These `NamedArray` elements are julia `MCMCChains`, which correspond to a specific set of effector, target, candidate model, and effector-to-target ratio. The `Chains` object is imported from the `Turing.jl` package.

There is an example SLURM script `slurm.sh` to run `example.jl`. This SLURM script calls `example.jl` 5 times with different command-line arguments. The five output files must be concatenated into a `5x2x2x8x4` `NamedArray` for further processing. An accompanying repo has an already computed version named `2023-09-19_cat_named_chains.jld2`.

The `pruning.jl` reads the `5x2x2x8x4` `NamedArray` and plots the chains that have not converged based on the R-hat statistic defined by Gelman et al. The script will plot chains for cases not meeting convergence criteria for manual inspection. Users can decide which chains to keep. The kept chains from `2023-09-19_cat_named_chains.jld2` are saved as a `5x2x2x8x4` array in `keep_chains.jld2`.

The `plot.jl` generates Figures 2-5 and all supplementary figures of the manuscript; the corresponding plot functions are defined in `plotting_functions.jl`. Figures 1 and 6 are generated using Mathematica notebook with the same name, i.e., `figure_1.nb` and `figure_6.nb`.
 
*NOTE: Figs. 4 and 5 in `plot.jl` are Supplementary Figs. 7 and 8.*
